rebuilds.why: Two distractors described the sight itself (the portraits; the ironical greeting), and since being spared the sight is the stated reason for gladness (l.19-20), the portrait one was defensible and the irony one only less obviously so. A small repair cannot fix a stem that admits the sight as a reason, so the question is reframed on the same lines, same type and tier: how the narrator thinks the King would have taken the sight. Key reworded to match ('perhaps' kept as 'might'); portrait option replaced by the negation-dropped reading of line 21; the request option replaced by one the passage contradicts. hintCore referred to the old options and is now a move. walkScript misquoted l.20 as 'a hot temper'; it now paraphrases the text's 'quick temper' as 'a man who was easily angered' (the scanner bars 'quick' in child-facing text, so the passage word cannot be quoted).
